name: OpenTelemetry
summary: A vendor-neutral observability specification organized around telemetry signals, context propagation, semantic conventions, and replaceable SDK/exporter boundaries.

features.name: Common telemetry signal data models
features.description: OpenTelemetry specifies interoperable models for traces, metrics, and logs, with signal-specific records such as spans and metric data carrying identity, attributes, timestamps, and relationships appropriate to each signal.
benefits: Provides a shared vocabulary across instrumentation and backends
Keeps signal semantics explicit at SDK and transport boundaries
costs: Implementations must preserve signal-specific semantics and cardinality constraints
A common model does not remove backend-specific feature differences

features.name: Distributed context propagation
features.description: The Context API and propagation specifications define a mechanism for carrying execution context across API boundaries, including trace and baggage information, so related operations can be correlated across processes.
benefits: Connects spans and related telemetry across service boundaries
Separates correlation state from a particular transport or exporter
costs: Propagation depends on correct instrumentation and carrier handling
Context leakage or unbounded baggage can affect correctness and resource use

features.name: SDK processing and exporter pipeline
features.description: OpenTelemetry SDKs provide configurable processing and export boundaries between instrumentation-produced telemetry and exporters that send data to external systems.
benefits: Allows batching, filtering, and export policy to vary independently of instrumentation
Supports multiple exporter protocols and destinations
costs: Queues and batching introduce delay and memory pressure
Exporter configuration and backend compatibility remain operational concerns

mathematical_views.question: How can trace, metric, and log records be composed from instrument identity, attributes, time, and signal-specific relationships?
assumptions: Signal records obey the specification's identity and validity rules
Backend storage and sampling are abstracted
Semantic conventions are treated as named vocabulary rather than proof of equivalence

mathematical_views.question: How does correlation context flow through a graph of process and transport boundaries?
assumptions: Instrumentation extracts and injects context at each boundary
Carrier encoding preserves the required propagation fields
The model abstracts sampling and clock uncertainty

mathematical_views.question: Which processing and export policies preserve acceptable signal delivery under batching, backpressure, and exporter failure?
assumptions: The view does not claim losslessness unless an implementation documents it

costs: Signal and backend differences require explicit mapping
Correctness depends on every participating boundary
Buffering, retries, and exporter configuration add operational state
